budgets.area: landing loop: queue, compose, check, settle
budgets.source: Dogfood main, 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-09, 491 accepted landings (landings read, submittedAt to committedAt): p50 16.1 min, best day 8.9, busiest day 23.2.
budgets.reason: Set at the 90th percentile of the rolling 20-landing median over those 7 days (25.2 min), so it breaks only in the slowest tenth of windows, with ten builders landing at once. It is a regression guard, not the goal; ratchet it down as the loop gets faster.

budgets.reason: Set at the 90th percentile of the rolling 20-landing p90 (60.1 min). The 2026-11-05 stall and 2026-11-08 queue waves are the windows it would have caught.

budgets.area: hosted check run
budgets.source: Accepting check runs of 45 landings sampled evenly across the same week (run summary wallSeconds): p50 8.3 min, 35 full and 10 scoped runs alike.

budgets.area: hosted check run
budgets.source: Same 45 sampled runs: p90 10.7 min, one outlier at 17.4.
budgets.reason: Observed p90 plus about 30%: one slow run in a 20-landing window must not break it (the p90 of 20 is the second slowest).

budgets.area: landing supervisor: check result to commit
budgets.source: Issue 03a749a5 (folded into b7851c44): the gap from check result (ciEndedAt) to the landing commit (committedAt) was 300 s before fix caa934a7 and measured 8.5 s live after it; stamped on every landing.
budgets.reason: The lead's bar: at most 30 s, per landing. Judged as the p90 of the last 20 landings, so the second slowest of 20 must be within 30 s and one stall cannot hide, but one outlier does not break it alone. A repeat of the 300 s gap breaks it within three landings.

budgets.area: unsaved-work snapshot: added to a Forge command, no changed file
budgets.source: Issue 7ac4e32f part 2, 2026-11-10, a hosted Lane checkout of a fresh import of this repo (4,210 files) on the dev deployment. Launching the snapshot worker inside a real CLI command added p50 2.4 ms, p90 5.9 ms, max 11 ms (25 commands); node scripts/perf-harness.mjs --snapshot-lane measured p50 1.1 ms, p90 1.5 ms (25 launches). Before, when the snapshot ran in the command's process, the walk of the same tree took p50 129 ms, p90 144 ms warm (138 ms in a fresh process), which is why the work moved to a detached worker.
budgets.reason: The lead's bar: single-op parity with git, so a command with nothing to snapshot adds under 50 ms. Judged on the p90 of the harness samples. The worker's own time (about 0.8 s of CPU per launch, at most one per 3 seconds per Lane) is background cost, not command latency.

budgets.area: unsaved-work snapshot: added to a Forge command, one or fifty changed files
budgets.source: Same checkout. Launching the worker with one changed file inside a real CLI command added p50 3.1 ms, p90 12.1 ms (max 26); with fifty changed files p50 4.2 ms, p90 16.2 ms (max 62); 25 commands each. perf-harness --snapshot-lane, one and fifty files together: p50 1.5 ms, p90 6.9 ms (50 launches). The snapshot is durable about 1.0 s (one file) and 1.9 s (fifty) after the command ends. Before, in the command's process: one file p50 808 ms, p90 920 ms; fifty files p50 1,665 ms, p90 1,818 ms.
budgets.reason: The lead's bar: a changed snapshot must not block a command for more than 300 ms at p90. Set to that bar, not to the measured numbers, because the cost is a process spawn and moves with machine load.

budgets.area: landing attempts: compose and check or reuse, per landing
budgets.source: Dogfood main 2026-11-08 to 11-10, 285 accepted landings (landings read): distinct Candidates per landing (recomposeCount + 1) averaged 2.26, its rolling 20-landing mean ranged 1.2 to 3.55 (p90 2.9). Stamped from the accepted attempt from this change on.
budgets.reason: Every attempt is a compose and a check or reuse, the biggest per-landing cost multiplier after batching. Set just above the worst 20-landing window seen, so only a recompose or re-check loop (incident 10d253c6) breaks it. Ratchet down once 20 stamped landings show the real spread.

budgets.area: landing-state writes: landing-path mutations, per landing
budgets.source: Landing-state writes of the 36 landings that settled 2026-11-10 04:06Z to 08:31Z (status version + 1): 8 writes for a landing with one attempt, 12 with two, 20 to 22 with three; mean 11.1, rolling 20-landing mean 10.2 to 11.3. Cost guard fixture 2026-11-10: 7 writes solo, 14 with one recompose.
budgets.reason: Set from the live spread, with the attempts budget's own ceiling in mind: 8 writes plus 4 per extra attempt is 20 at 4 attempts, so 22 breaks on a write loop, not on a busy window the attempts budget allows. Ratchet down if a window of 20 stays below 14.

budgets.area: GitHub runner minutes of the accepted check (shard execution), per landing
budgets.source: Shard execution seconds of the check runs of the 36 landings that settled 2026-11-10 04:06Z to 08:31Z, from each run's stored summary (timings.executionSeconds); the live stamp is the same field of the run row, read when the landing sees the run end. Accepted check: mean 54.4 min, rolling 20-landing mean 49.2 to 57.0.
budgets.reason: Rolling peak 57.0 plus about 20% for a heavier test set. Free on our public repository; about $0.006 a minute at list price for a private one (capture #4), so 54 minutes is about $0.33 a landing. A shard plan that stops sharding, or a test set that doubles, breaks it.

budgets.source: Shard execution seconds of the check runs of the 36 landings that settled 2026-11-10 04:06Z to 08:31Z, from each run's stored summary (timings.executionSeconds); the live stamp is the same field of the run row, read when the landing sees the run end. Counts runs that ended with their shard seconds recorded; a run cancelled before it ended counts nothing.

costs.area: Convex queries on the landing path, per landing
costs.source: tests/landing-cost-guard.test.mjs on the in-process Convex fixture, 2026-11-10: one solo land --save, one whose main moves during its check (recompose on a source job and a second check), and four queued landings batched under the default policy; total divided by the 6 landings.
costs.reason: Queries the server runs for a landing without a client read. The client wait and the finish observer are live-only (about 31 executions per landing in capture #2); slice 1 cut their bytes. An extra read per landing fails here.

costs.source: tests/landing-cost-guard.test.mjs on the in-process Convex fixture, 2026-11-10: one solo land --save, one whose main moves during its check (recompose on a source job and a second check), and four queued landings batched under the default policy; total divided by the 6 landings.
costs.reason: Controller wakes, driver steps, check callbacks and acceptance. Slice 2 skipped controller wakes that cannot change eligibility; one batched CI result path per run (65534f20) is the next cut.

costs.area: Convex Node action executions (512 MiB), per landing
costs.source: tests/landing-cost-guard.test.mjs on the in-process Convex fixture, 2026-11-10: one solo land --save, one whose main moves during its check (recompose on a source job and a second check), and four queued landings batched under the default policy; total divided by the 6 landings.
costs.reason: Node source steps cost eight times a V8 step per second; capture #3 found them the top function after more steps per landing. Fewer source-job steps is the decision.

costs.reason: The queue throughput decision: runs per accepted landing at most 1.2 in the synthetic queue harness; check minutes follow runs. Live: 1.48 distinct runs per landing over 285 landings, 2026-11-08 to 11-10.

costs.area: whole-row reads of main's path history (projectHostedOverlapMain), per landing
costs.source: tests/landing-cost-guard.test.mjs on the in-process Convex fixture, 2026-11-10: the acceptance write that moves the row reads it once (5 reads over the 6 fixture landings). Before Issue 750c5929 the landing completion read and rewrote it again to name the landing (7 reads).
costs.reason: The row is 140 KB on Forge (2,852 paths, cap 128 KB of path entries). Landing names and Lanes behind main (save trial merge, overlap read) use the per-landing log instead; tests/hosted-overlaps.test.mjs fails if a save or overlap read of a Lane within the log window reads the whole row again.

costs.area: unsaved-work snapshot: R2 uploads for one changed file
costs.source: tests/hosted-lane-snapshots.test.mjs, 2026-11-10: a changed packed snapshot (a CLI with lane-snapshot-packs, deployed by 7ac4e32f) uploads one pack holding the page and every changed file; unchanged files are never sent. The loose path it replaced uploaded 2.
costs.reason: A snapshot runs per command with changes, so it is charged per edit, not per landing. One pack per snapshot; any extra upload fails. The two-upload loose path is no longer the baseline.

costs.area: unsaved-work snapshot: Convex calls for one changed file
costs.source: tests/hosted-lane-snapshots.test.mjs, 2026-11-10: a changed packed snapshot is one prepare call and no commit (the entry is live after prepare); an unchanged tree costs no call. The loose path it replaced was prepare and commit.
costs.reason: One call per changed snapshot and zero when nothing changed; any extra call fails.

costs.area: GitHub Actions wall minutes of a landing's checks (latency, not runner minutes)
costs.source: Dogfood main 2026-11-08 to 11-10: 421 distinct check runs for 285 accepted landings (1.48 per landing, landings read) times the check p50 of 8.3 min (speed budget check-p50). This is wall time, one run's shards running side by side: the runner minutes behind it are the next entry (capture #4: stored shard seconds 77.9 min per landing, mostly 12 shards of about 4.5 min each per run).
costs.reason: Kept for the queue-throughput and latency decisions; judged live by check-p50/p90 and attempts, and on change by landing-check-runs. Do not read it as cost: price follows check-runner-minutes.

costs.area: GitHub Actions runner minutes of a landing's checks (shard execution, summed over shards)
costs.source: Check results of the 36 landings that settled 2026-11-10 04:06Z to 08:31Z (landings read, then the stored run summary of each run: timings.executionSeconds, the shard execution seconds the run row keeps). Per landing: accepted check 54.4 min (rolling 20-landing mean 49.2 to 57.0, 10 to 12 shards, one scoped run of 2), runs its attempts discarded 4.7 (2.5 to 5.9), the main audit that followed 18.8 (13.3 to 23.4; 12 audit runs shared by 36 landings, counted once). Live since this change: budgets landing-runner-accepted-mean, landing-runner-discarded-mean and landing-runner-audit-mean.
costs.reason: Capture #4 measured about 113 GitHub runner minutes per landing (1,110 exact by job interval in a 56.9 min window with 10 landings; $0 billed on our public repository, about $681 per 1,000 landings at list price for a private repository). Of those, 86.4 are the forge-check runs (accepted 53.8, discarded 5.5, audit 11.4, check-only and cancelled runs that never became a landing 15.7), 22.0 are this repository's own Verify Forge workflow on each push (not a user's check), 2.6 deploy, sign and smoke. The stored shard seconds (77.9, a 36-landing window) are about 90% of the forge-check minutes (86.4, a 10-landing window); the rest is the plan and static jobs, setup before the shards and runs no landing owns.

costs.area: agent put-planning-item on an existing Issue: Convex calls per write
costs.source: tests/hosted-agent-planning.test.mjs and tests/hosted-contention.test.mjs on the in-process Convex fixture, 2026-11-10: one revision-free mutation (projectWorkCommand:command). Before flip 5 S5 it was 1 workspace query plus 1 action with about 8 inner calls, and 3.0% of puts repeated all of it after an unrelated write.
costs.reason: A planning write is one mutation whose only check is its item version (ITEM_CHANGED); a revision read or retry loop coming back fails here.

costs.area: agent comment-planning-item: Convex calls per write
costs.source: tests/hosted-agent-planning.test.mjs and tests/hosted-contention.test.mjs on the in-process Convex fixture, 2026-11-10: one revision-free mutation (flip 5 S0). Before: 1 workspace query plus 1 action with about 8 inner calls.
costs.reason: Comments are insert-only and need no revision; any extra call per comment fails.

costs.area: Work queries re-run per planning write, three open tabs
costs.source: tests/hosted-agent-planning.test.mjs and tests/hosted-contention.test.mjs on the in-process Convex fixture, 2026-11-10: the flip 5 re-run meter (10 subscriptions per tab) gives 2 per tab for a new Issue, a status change, a comment and a note; the worst write times three tabs. Before: 3 per tab (9), the workspace query re-ran on every write.
costs.reason: The workspace query is the heaviest read and must not depend on the project-wide Work revision again; one more re-run per tab fails.

costs.area: Search-index queries per planning search and per new-Issue duplicate check
costs.source: tests/hosted-agent-planning.test.mjs on the in-process Convex fixture, 2026-11-10: one CLI planning search and one new Issue (its likelyDuplicates check) each run one withSearchIndex query; ordinary rows add no per-result search.
costs.reason: Convex bills every text search at the whole search-index size, whatever the limit or filters (planning-search-billed-bytes); a second search per operation doubles that, so any rise fails.

costs.area: Billed search bytes (query-GB) per search_planning query on dogfood
costs.source: convex logs --success sample, 2026-11-10 (Issue a02991a7): textIndexQueryBytes 7.47 MB for every projectHostedPlanningSearch:search, projectHostedFriction:capture and projectWorkIndex:workspace search. Convex docs (search/text-search#costs) and convex-backend usage_tracking: each query counts the full on-disk size of the index, once per search.
costs.reason: Billed as Search queries at $0.11 per 1,000 query-GB (Starter), about $0.0000008 per search and $0.0008 a day at 920 searches; it grows with every projectWorkRecords row of every generation, not with the limit. Judged on change by planning-index-searches.

costs.area: Save-time trial merge: full overlap-row reads for a truncated disjoint peer, per save
costs.source: tests/hosted-trial-merge.test.mjs: a 40-path disjoint peer reads zero full overlap rows; legacy rows without the optional filter stay conservative, and an omitted shared path still gets the same trial merge. Synthetic DB bytes are metered, not billed usage.
costs.reason: Replaces unconditional full-row reads for truncated peers with a 512-character all-path filter. At the capture #4 mix (60,000 old peer bytes/save, 1.6 head moves/landing), 1,000 landings avoid 96 MB of peer rows before false positives and rollout. At a full 51-row presence window the added field costs at most about 27 KB/save, leaving about 53 MB net read savings/1,000 landings; shared peers, false positives, writes and other presence reads reduce the net. Calls unchanged; idle zero.

costs.area: Landing driver advance at 1,000 test files / 10 shards
costs.source: Dogfood landing fixture: one solo passed landing, 1,000 synthetic retained reports and ten shards; 274 KB run value. Before 606,839 B, one duplicate 286,568 B row read removed.
costs.reason: Reuses the canonical run already read in the same transaction; keeps current authority, configuration and exact evidence checks. No extra calls or tables.
